identity.fantasy: A battlefield alchemist who combines Ingredients, Bases, and Mojos to change what every Cauldron and Potion Toss does.
identity.one_line: A battlefield alchemist who combines Ingredients, Bases, and Mojos to change what every Cauldron and Potion Toss does. The defining decision is contextual: Movement, triage, and utility side effects change Potion Toss and ward decisions.

mechanics.core_loop: A modular alchemist healer. Ingredients, Bases, and Mojos change the effects of the Cauldron and Potion Toss, so the player prepares the right brew for steady healing, shields, raid healing, or damage support. It is flexible and utility-rich, but less plug-and-play than a conventional direct healer.

modes.name: Tiki Splash
modes.structural_description: While a Base is active, Spirit in a Bottle will now transform into Tiki Splash.Tiki SplashSplash target location with healing waters, healing for 34 + 25% SP every 1 sec for 5 seconds. Gains a new effect based on your currently active Base. Scales with modifiers to Spirit in a Bottle.Beast Blood: Grants you 5% increased critical strike chance for 15 seconds, stacking 2 times.Crystal Water: Grants you a shield that absorbs 422 + 75% SP Magic damage for 15 seconds.

mechanics.single_target: Maintain the selected Ingredient, Base, and Mojo recipe, place Cauldron where allies can use it, and Potion Toss the moving tank while contributing damage when healing is stable.
mechanics.aoe: Use Cauldron and recipe effects for group coverage, but account for slow effigy behavior and the Stasis Ward stun. Current healers describe both passive ease and meaningful recipe nuance.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Hybrid range and throwable tools support movement, while persistent devices reward planned placement.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Its structural defensive package includes Ingredient, Potion Toss, Potent Mixes, Spirit Healer, Splash Potion.
mechanics.group_utility: Group or control tools include Ingredient, Mixologist, Ingredient, Ingredient, Loa's Blessing.

failure_modes.text: The wrong recipe, poor Cauldron placement, a slow effigy, or an unnoticed Stasis Ward stun can make the prepared toolkit answer the wrong emergency.
A Cauldron placed behind a moving group cannot deliver the recipe selected for the pull.
Ignoring an effigy's travel time or Stasis Ward's stun can make a nominally available tool arrive too late or disrupt the wrong moment.
